commands.author: maweibin

target.title: fix(status): remove dead-code `|| 1` fallback in channel status display
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/commands/status-all/channels.ts` uses `accounts.length || 1` and `enabledAccounts.length || 1` in three display-formatting branches. The `|| 1` fallback is **dead code** — the value can never be `0` at any of the three evaluation points because every reachable path is guarded by a condition that guarantees `length >= 1`.

Dead fallback code is a **maintenance hazard**: it signals to future readers that `0` is a possible value here, which is false. A future refactor that changes the guard condition could silently rely on this fallback and introduce a real bug.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the three dead `|| 1` fallbacks so the invariant is explicit. Each location is protected as follows:

| Line | Expression | Why `0` is unreachable |
|------|-----------|------------------------|
| 383 | `accounts.length \|\| 1` | Entering this branch requires `accounts.length > 1 \|\| forceAccountBinding`. When `accounts.length === 0`, `anyEnabled` is `false` (line 283: `[].some(...)` returns `false`), and the `!anyEnabled` guard at line 361 returns `"disabled"` **before** reaching this expression. |
| 402 | `accounts.length \|\| 1` | Same `!anyEnabled` early-return guard as line 383. |
| 423 | `enabledAccounts.length \|\| 1` | Reaching line 423 requires `configuredAccounts.length > 0` (line 418). `configuredAccounts` is `enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured)` (line 285), so `enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length > 0`. |

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. The three expressions produce the same output with or without `|| 1` because the fallback is never triggered. Purely a code-quality cleanup that eliminates misleading dead code.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout, Node v24.13.1, PR head.

**Proof — focused regression test exercises the changed expressions via `forceAccountBinding` gate:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts --run

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

New test "renders account count via forceAccountBinding gate (exercises accounts.length, not dead || 1)":
- Configures a channel plugin with `forceAccountBinding: true`, 1 enabled+configured account
- Calls the real `buildChannelsTable()` — the production function from this branch
- Asserts `expect(row?.detail).toContain("accounts 1")` — proving the changed expressions ARE reached
- Output is `"accounts 1"` with or without `|| 1` — the fix changes nothing for the output

```
$ npx oxlint src/commands/status-all/channels.ts src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts
→ exit 0
```

**What was not tested:** `openclaw status --all` CLI end-to-end. The vitest test exercises the same `buildChannelsTable` function with forceAccountBinding, reaching the same three changed expressions the CLI would hit.

## Regression Test Plan

- `$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts --run` — **1 passed, 10 tests passed** (9 existing + 1 new forceAccountBinding test)
- `$ npx oxlint src/commands/status-all/channels.ts src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts` — **0 errors**
- `$ git diff --stat` — **2 files, +28/-3**

## Root Cause

In `buildChannelsTable()`, three display-formatting branches append `accounts ${N}` strings with `N || 1` as a defensive fallback. However, each evaluation point is **control-flow guarded** by a condition that structurally prevents `N === 0`: the `!anyEnabled` guard (line 361) returns `"disabled"` before reaching lines 382-403, and the `configuredAccounts.length > 0` guard (line 418) guarantees `enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length > 0` via the subset relation (line 285). The `|| 1` was a defensive pattern added without tracing the full control flow.
